title: Construction of three novel Ln3 compounds using multidentate Schiff base ligand: Crystal structures, fluorescence properties, and biological activities

synthesis.procedure: Shared solvothermal synthesis for compounds 1–3: Nd(dbm)3·2H2O (0.025 mmol, 0.0213 g) was added to a solution of HL (0.025 mmol, 0.008 g) in 15 mL CH3OH/CH2Cl2 (v/v = 2:1). The mixture was stirred for 30 min at room temperature, sealed in a 20 mL glass sample vase, and heated at 80 °C for 24 h under autogenous pressure, then cooled to room temperature. Yellow block crystals suitable for single-crystal X-ray diffraction were obtained.

synthesis.time: 30 min stirring then 24 h solvothermal heating
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solvothermal reaction in a sealed 20 mL glass sample vase under autogenous pressure
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: cooled to room temperature; yellow block crystals obtained

properties.summary: Compound 1 shows typical NIR Nd(III) luminescence at room temperature. When excited at 404 nm, emission peaks appear at 918, 1051, 1061, 1317 and 1343 nm. The fluorescence lifetime is 7.03 μs. UV–vis spectra of 1–3 in methanol show ligand-based absorptions with coordination-induced shifts.

properties.summary: Compound 2 displays typical Sm(III) NIR and visible luminescence at room temperature. NIR emission peaks at 909, 933, 950, 961, 1030 and 1175 nm appear upon 365 nm excitation. Solid-state visible emission under 286 nm excitation shows peaks at 486, 539, 598 and 645 nm assigned to Sm(III) 4G5/2 → 6HJ transitions. The fluorescence lifetime is 9.75 μs.
